proposals.zh: 明年正月，賈后又使黃門自首，欲與太子為逆。

fields.before: Next New Year Jia staged a Yellow Gate confession implicating Yu.
fields.after: In the first month of the following year, Empress Jia again had a palace eunuch confess that he had intended to rebel with the crown prince.

proposals.zh: 詔以黃門首辭班示公卿。

fields.before: Luoyang read the staged confession.
fields.after: An edict circulated the eunuch’s confession among the dukes and ministers.

proposals.zh: 又遣澹以千兵防送太子，更幽于許昌宮之別坊，令治書御史劉振持節守之。

fields.before: Dan convoyed Yu to Xuchang under guard.
fields.after: Jia also sent Dan with a thousand soldiers to escort the crown prince to a separate compound of the Xuchang palace, and ordered Liu Zhen, an imperial censor, to guard him with a tally of authority.

proposals.zh: 南風，后名；

fields.before: South Wind' was the empress's name.
fields.after: “South wind” was the empress’s name.

fields.before: South Wind' meant Empress Jia.
fields.after: “South wind” referred to the empress’s name.

proposals.zh: 初，太子之廢也，妃父王衍表請離婚。

fields.before: Wang Yan filed for divorce the moment Yu fell.
fields.after: When the crown prince was first deposed, his consort’s father, Wang Yan, petitioned for their divorce.

proposals.zh: 雖非中宮所生，奉事有如親母。

fields.before: He claimed dutiful service to Jia despite birth.
fields.after: Though I was not born to the empress, I served her as I would my own mother.

proposals.zh: 自為太子以來，敕見禁檢，不得見母。

fields.before: Palace rules barred him from Lady Xie.
fields.after: Since becoming crown prince, I have been confined by imperial orders and have not been allowed to see my mother.

proposals.zh: 自宜城君亡，不見存恤，恆在空室中坐。

fields.before: Since Princess Dowager Xuan city died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.
fields.after: Since the Lady of Yicheng died, I have received no comfort or care and have constantly sat alone in an empty room.

fields.before: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.
fields.after: Since the Lady of Yicheng died, I have received no comfort or care and have constantly sat alone in an empty room.

proposals.zh: 去年十二月，道文疾病困篤，父子之情，實相憐湣。

fields.before: He mourned son Daowen's fatal illness.
fields.after: In the twelfth month of last year, Daowen’s illness became grave, and the bond between father and son made me grieve deeply for him.

proposals.zh: 于時表國家乞加徽號，不見聽許。

fields.before: His plea for son's title failed.
fields.after: At that time I petitioned the throne to bestow an honorific title on him, but my request was refused.

proposals.zh: 疾病既篤，為之求請恩福，無有噁心。

fields.before: He denied malice in praying for the boy.
fields.after: When his illness became grave, I sought blessings for him; I had no evil intention.

proposals.zh: 自道文病，中宮三遣左右來視，云：'天教呼汝。

fields.before: Palace runners claimed Heaven summoned Yu.
fields.after: After Daowen fell ill, the empress sent attendants to see me three times, saying, “His Majesty has summoned you.”

proposals.zh: '到二十八日暮，有短函來，題言東宮發，疏云：'言天教欲見汝。

fields.before: A cryptic note echoed the summons.
fields.after: On the evening of the twenty-eighth, a short letter arrived, marked as an Eastern Palace dispatch, saying that His Majesty wished to see me.

proposals.zh: '即便作表求入。

fields.before: He requested audience.
fields.after: I immediately prepared a memorial requesting permission to enter.

proposals.zh: 二十九日早入見國家，須臾遣至中宮。

fields.before: He saw Hui briefly then reached Jia's halls.
fields.after: Early on the twenty-ninth, I entered and saw His Majesty; shortly afterward I was sent to the empress’s quarters.

proposals.zh: 中宮左右陳舞見語：'中宮旦來吐不快。

fields.before: Inner attendants Chen Wu told him: 'The empress vomited ill this morning.'
fields.after: The empress’s attendant Chen Wu told me, “The empress has been unwell and vomited this morning.”

fields.before: Chen Wu claimed Jia was sick.
fields.after: The empress’s attendant Chen Wu told me, “The empress has been unwell and vomited this morning.”

proposals.zh: '使住空屋中坐。

fields.before: She told you to wait seated in an empty chamber.
fields.after: They made me sit and wait in an empty room.

fields.before: They parked him in an empty room.
fields.after: They made me sit and wait in an empty room.

proposals.zh: '中宮遙呼陳舞：'昨天教與太子酒棗。

fields.before: The empress called Chen Wu from afar: Yesterday I ordered wine and jujubes given the crown prince.
fields.after: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: “Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes to be given to the crown prince.”

fields.before: Jia recalled forcing wine earlier.
fields.after: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: “Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes to be given to the crown prince.”

proposals.zh: '便持三升酒、大盤棗來見與，使飲酒啖棗盡。

fields.before: She brought three sheng of ale and a great tray of jujubes and made him finish both.
fields.after: Chen Wu then brought three sheng of wine and a large tray of jujubes to me and made me drink and eat them all.

fields.before: Chen Wu forced three sheng wine and dates.
fields.after: Chen Wu brought me three sheng of wine and a large tray of jujubes and made me finish them.

proposals.zh: 鄙素不飲酒，即便遣舞啟說不堪三升之意。

fields.before: Yu pleaded low tolerance.
fields.after: I had never been accustomed to drinking wine, so I sent Chen Wu to explain that I could not manage three sheng.

proposals.zh: 中宮遙呼曰：'汝常陛下前持酒可喜，何以不飲？

fields.before: Jia taunted his earlier drinking.
fields.after: The empress called from a distance, “You have often taken wine gladly before His Majesty. Why will you not drink it now?”

proposals.zh: 天與汝酒，當使道文差也。

fields.before: She tied drinking to son's health.
fields.after: “His Majesty has given you wine to help Daowen recover.”

proposals.zh: '便答中宮：'陛下會同一日見賜，故不敢辭，通日不飲三升酒也。

fields.before: Yu cited earlier imperial banquet.
fields.after: I replied to the empress, “His Majesty gave me wine on one occasion, and I did not dare refuse it; but even in a whole day I do not drink three sheng.”

proposals.zh: 且實未食，恐不堪。

fields.before: Empty stomach worried him.
fields.after: “Besides, I have not eaten, and I fear I cannot bear it.”

proposals.zh: 又未見殿下，飲此或至顛倒。

fields.before: He feared drunken copying.
fields.after: “And I have not yet seen Your Highness; if I drink this, I may become disoriented.”

proposals.zh: '陳舞復傳語云：'不孝那！

fields.before: Chen Wu called him unfilial.
fields.after: Chen Wu relayed another message: “How unfilial!”

proposals.zh: 天與汝酒飲，不肯飲，中有惡物邪？

fields.before: She accused refusal of hiding guilt.
fields.after: “His Majesty gives you wine, and you will not drink it. Is there something bad in it?”

proposals.zh: '遂可飲二升，餘有一升，求持還東宮飲盡。

fields.before: Then you may drink two sheng—leave one sheng to carry back to Eastern Palace and finish.
fields.after: I managed to drink two sheng; with one sheng left, I asked to take it back to the Eastern Palace and finish it there.

fields.before: They compromised at two sheng plus one to go.
fields.after: I managed to drink two sheng. With one sheng left, I asked to take it back to the Eastern Palace and finish it there.

proposals.zh: 逼迫不得已，更飲一升。

fields.before: Pressed helplessly he drank another sheng.
fields.after: Under pressure and with no choice, I drank another sheng.

fields.before: Cornered he drank more.
fields.after: Pressed and unable to refuse, I drank another sheng.

proposals.zh: 飲已，體中荒迷，不復自覺。

fields.before: After drinking his body grew confused and he lost awareness.
fields.after: After drinking, I became confused and no longer knew what I was doing.

fields.before: He blacked out—the forged edict followed.
fields.after: After drinking, I became confused and no longer knew what I was doing.

proposals.zh: 須臾有一小婢持封箱來，云：'詔使寫此文書。

fields.before: A girl delivered a case—'copy this edict.'
fields.after: Soon a young maid brought a sealed case and said, “An edict orders you to copy this document.”

proposals.zh: '鄙便驚起，視之，有一白紙，一青紙。

fields.before: He found white and green paper inside.
fields.after: I sprang up in alarm and saw one sheet of white paper and one of green paper.

proposals.zh: 催促云：'陛下停待。

fields.before: Runners said the emperor waited.
fields.after: They urged me on, saying, “His Majesty is waiting.”

proposals.zh: 急疾不容復視，實不覺紙上語輕重。

fields.before: Rush left no time to read the forgery's sense.
fields.after: They hurried me so I could not look it over again; I truly did not realize the significance of the words on the paper.

proposals.zh: 父母至親，實不相疑，事理如此，實為見誣，想眾人見明也。」

fields.before: He closed pleading filial trust and public innocence.'
fields.after: “Parents are one’s closest kin, and I did not doubt them. This is how it happened: I have truly been falsely accused, and I trust that everyone will see the truth.”

proposals.zh: 太子既廢非其罪，眾情憤怨。

fields.before: Injustice against Yu enraged the capital.
fields.after: The crown prince had been deposed for no fault of his own, and people were indignant.

proposals.zh: 右衛督司馬雅，宗室之疏屬也，與常從督許超並有寵于太子，二人深傷之，說趙王倫謀臣孫秀曰：「國無適嗣，社稷將危，大臣之禍必起。

fields.before: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Prince Zhao of Lun: 'The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.
fields.after: Sima Ya, a commandant of the Right Guard and a distant member of the imperial clan, and Xu Chao, a commandant of the regular attendants, both enjoyed the crown prince’s favor. Deeply grieved, they spoke to Sun Xiu, an adviser to Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao: “The state has no rightful heir, the altars of soil and grain will be endangered, and disaster will surely arise for the great ministers.”

fields.before: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Prince Zhao of Lun: "The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.
fields.after: Sima Ya, a Right Guard commandant and distant member of the imperial clan, and Xu Chao, a commandant of the regular attendants, were both favored by the crown prince. Deeply grieved, they told Sun Xiu, an adviser to Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao: “The state has no rightful heir; the dynasty is in danger, and disaster will surely come upon the great ministers.”

proposals.zh: 而公奉事中宮，與賈后親密，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一旦事起，禍必及矣。

fields.before: They warned Sun Xiu that Jia would scapegoat Jia's allies.
fields.after: “You serve the empress and are close to her; everyone says you knew of the crown prince’s deposition beforehand. If trouble breaks out, disaster will certainly reach you.”

proposals.zh: 秀言于趙王倫，倫深納焉。

fields.before: Xiu reported to Prince Zhao of Lun, and Lun accepted fully.
fields.after: Xiu told Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, who readily accepted the plan.

fields.before: Sun Xiu sold the plot to Sima Lun.
fields.after: Sun Xiu told Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, who readily accepted the plan.

proposals.zh: 計既定，而秀說倫曰：「太子為人剛猛，若得志之日，必肆其情性矣。

fields.before: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, 'The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.
fields.after: Once the plan was settled, Xiu said to Lun, “The crown prince is by nature strong and fierce; if he achieves his aims, he will surely give free rein to his disposition.”

fields.before: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, "The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.
fields.after: Once the plan was settled, Sun Xiu said to Lun, “The crown prince is strong and fierce by nature; if he achieves his aims, he will surely give free rein to his disposition.”

proposals.zh: 明公素事賈后，街談巷議，皆以公為賈氏之黨。

fields.before: Lun was branded Jia's man.
fields.after: “You have long served Empress Jia, and people in the streets all call you a partisan of the Jia family.”

proposals.zh: 今雖欲建大功于太子，太子雖將含忍宿忿，必不能加賞於公，當謂公逼百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳。

fields.before: Yu would not thank Lun for a late defection.
fields.after: “Even if you now seek to do the crown prince a great service, though he might suppress his old resentment, he will surely not reward you. He will think you changed sides under pressure from public opinion only to escape punishment.”

proposals.zh: 若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。

fields.before: One slip and Lun's head would roll.
fields.after: “At the first pretext, you still will not escape execution.”

proposals.zh: 秀因使反間，言殿中人欲廢賈后，迎太子。

fields.before: Sun Xiu spread rumors of a palace plot to restore Yu.
fields.after: Sun Xiu then spread a misleading report that men in the palace intended to depose Empress Jia and bring the crown prince back.

proposals.zh: 賈后聞之憂怖，乃使太醫令程據合巴豆杏子丸。

fields.before: Jia panicked and had Cheng Ju mix purgative poison.
fields.after: When Empress Jia heard this, she was frightened and ordered the chief imperial physician Cheng Ju to prepare croton and apricot-kernel pills.

proposals.zh: 三月，矯詔使黃門孫慮齋至許昌以害太子。

fields.before: Third month a fake edict sent Sun Lü to kill Yu at Xuchang.
fields.after: In the third month, a forged edict sent the palace eunuch Sun Lü to Xuchang to kill the crown prince.

proposals.zh: 初，太子恐見鴆，恆自煮食於前。

fields.before: Yu had cooked for himself to avoid cup poison.
fields.after: The crown prince had earlier feared being poisoned and always cooked his own food in front of himself.

proposals.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子于小坊中，絕不與食，宮中猶於牆壁上過食與太子。

fields.before: Lü jailed and starved Yu; sympathizers smuggled food over walls.
fields.after: Sun Lü told Liu Zhen, who moved the crown prince to a small compound and cut off his food. People in the palace nevertheless passed food to him over the wall.

proposals.zh: 慮乃逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，因如廁，慮以藥杵椎殺之，太子大呼，聲聞於外。

fields.before: Sun Lü beat Yu to death in the latrine with a pestle—screams escaped.
fields.after: Sun Lü then forced the medicine on the crown prince, who refused to take it. When the prince went to the privy, Sun Lü beat him to death with a medicine pestle; his cries were heard outside.

proposals.zh: 時年二十三。

fields.before: He died at twenty-three.
fields.after: He was twenty-three by traditional reckoning.

proposals.zh: 此志不遂，重以酸恨。

fields.before: She claimed thwarted maternal hopes.
fields.after: “That wish has come to nothing, deepening my grief and regret.”

proposals.zh: 遹雖罪在莫大，猶王者子孫，便以匹庶送終，情實憐湣，特乞天恩，賜以王禮。

fields.before: She asked royal burial despite his crimes.
fields.after: “Though Yu’s crime was very great, he was still a descendant of the imperial house. I cannot help pitying him if he is buried as a commoner, and I especially beg imperial grace to grant him the rites of a prince.”

proposals.zh: 詔以廣陵王禮葬之。

fields.before: The court buried him as Guangling prince.
fields.after: An edict ordered that he be buried with the rites of the Prince of Guangling.
